question: Assume today is 2026-09-11. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the total number of passengers who used public transport in Spain in August 2026 (urban, interurban and special/discretionary transport combined), as it will be first reported in the provisional data of the National Statistics Institute's (INE) Passenger Transport Statistics (Estadística de Transporte de Personas).

target.what: Total number of passenger journeys reported by the Instituto Nacional de Estadística (INE) Passenger Transport Statistics (Estadística de Transporte de Personas) for Spain, summing urban, interurban and special/discretionary transport, as first published in the provisional release for August 2026.
target.cadence: Monthly; first provisional release, with possible later revisions.
target.caveats: Working interpretation: counts passenger boardings/journeys, not unique people; sums the three published ETP categories urban, interurban and special/discretionary, using the modes and operators covered by INE. Private car, informal transport, and possibly some taxi/ride-hailing activity are outside

candidates.hypothesis: The August 2026 ETP total will be close to the August 2025 total adjusted by the 2026 level/trend; the August month-of-year ratio and category mix are stable enough to project from prior Augusts and any 2026 months published before the cutoff.
candidates.data_to_find: INE ETP monthly total passengers for Spain, sum of urban, interurban and special/discretionary transport, for August 2021-2025 and any 2026 months published up to July 2026; also August 2024 and August 2025 component totals and the latest 3-6 monthly totals. Minimum evidence: August 2025 total plus at least one 2026 monthly total or annual growth rate.

candidates.hypothesis: Monthly passenger counts from major Spanish operators (Metro Madrid, TMB Barcelona, EMT Madrid, Renfe Cercanías, FGC, Metro Bilbao, Valencia/Seville consortia) for August 2026 or July 2026, compared with August 2025, can serve as leading indicators for national urban/interurban ridership after scaling by their national ETP share.
candidates.data_to_find: Operator monthly passenger counts for July/August 2026 and August 2025; operator shares of national ETP urban and interurban passenger totals. Minimum evidence: at least several large operators covering a substantial share, with comparable 2025 and 2026 periods.

candidates.hypothesis: August public transport demand, especially interurban and urban services in tourist cities, is positively related to tourist overnight stays and airport arrivals; 2026 tourism growth versus 2025 can adjust the August seasonal projection.
candidates.data_to_find: AENA airport passenger statistics for August 2026 if published by the cutoff, INE hotel overnight stays/hotel occupancy for August 2026 or latest months, Frontur tourist arrivals, and comparable August 2025 values. Minimum evidence: year-on-year growth in at least one high-frequency tourist indicator for August 2026 or July 2026, plus a historical correlation/elasticity with ETP August passengers.

candidates.hypothesis: Passenger journeys equal provided service (vehicle-km, train-km, scheduled trips) multiplied by average occupancy; August 2026 service schedules and comparable occupancy rates can bound the national total if ridership history is unavailable.
candidates.data_to_find: August 2026 scheduled bus/metro/train service levels or vehicle-km for major operators and national aggregates, average occupancy rates from 2025 or operator reports, and coverage shares. Minimum evidence: service supply and occupancy for a large operator or region that can be scaled nationally with an explicit coverage assumption.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
